title: Women who defined an era
excerpt: Growing up in a Tamil household , the story of Ponniyin Selvan was a common thread in my life. Intrigued by its mystique, I found myself drawn into the captivating world crafted by Kalki.
body:
KUNDAVAI
 
Take Kundhavai for instance, a patriot who never waited for her prince to arrive on horseback to rescue her kingdom when her father was bedridden, her brother Aditha Karikalan, who was consumed in himself, or Arulmozhi Varman, who was least interested in the kingdom, she decided to take responsibility and navigate her kingdom through difficult times. Kundavai was never portrayed as Jhansi Rani or Teresa; instead, she was a princess with flaws like us.
  
Nandhini, the alluring antagonist, whose weapon of choice is not a sword but her beauty. Her beauty captivated every man who beheld her, leading them to pursue her relentlessly, willing to do whatever it took to win her favor. She experienced betrayal from those she trusted most, abandonment, and the ultimate anguish of having to harm the man she once loved dearly. Nonetheless, she was a product of her circumstances, as we are all of today!
 
Vaanathi, the shy and cliché princess is the woman grew stronger with each bully of Poonguzhali, and even decided to give up the throne to prove that her love is not shallow. Even the reason for her existence throughout the novel piqued my interest but yes, I was able to understand her over a period.

Poonguzhali , depicted as a fearless and strong women in “Ponniyin Selvan”, unafraid of the stormy sea’s raging waves. Poonguzhali is a strong woman who defies the society’s rules and bravely protects the prince despite her disdain for royalty. She sometimes says mean things to Vanathi, who she knows is weaker than her. Nevertheless, she one of the “most admired” among Kalki’s female characters.

It’s impossible to overlook Manimegalai, the epitome of selflessness in the novel. Though her character wasn’t featured in the movie adaptation, her journey is profoundly impactful. From a naive young girl to a woman who embraces spiritual surrender, her transformation is remarkable. Despite facing challenges and confusion due to her associations, her enduring love ultimately leads to her downfall. The series culminates with Manimegalai’s story, leaving a lasting imprint on the reader’s heart.
Ponniyin Selvan is a rare gem in which strong and resilient women hold authority. It’s a novel in which women aren’t just love interests or second fiddles to guys. Kalki’s portrayal of these women as masterminds of Rajathanthiram is breathtaking. Ponniyin Selvan is rightfully described as a celebration of womanhood.
“Cheers to the remarkable women who uplift, inspire, and shape our world every day. Happy International Women’s Day!”

title: i still remember my first email password
excerpt: Not because it was clever. Because choosing it felt like the first real decision the internet ever asked of me.
body: Not because it was clever. Because choosing it felt like the first real decision the internet ever asked of me — a little string of characters that was mine and nobody else's, typed carefully into a box that felt enormous at the time.
It's a small thing to be nostalgic about. But it was the first time a website asked me who I wanted to be, even a little, and I remember taking the question seriously.
I've forgotten that password. I haven't forgotten how it felt to make it up.

title: notes on doing nothing online
excerpt: An argument for the aimless browse — no destination, no feed, just clicking a link because the name of it was interesting.
body: An argument for the aimless browse — no destination, no feed, just clicking a link because the name of it was interesting, and then another, and then somehow forty minutes had passed and you'd learned about deep-sea creatures or a stranger's collection of vintage postcards.
That kind of wandering doesn't have a place to happen anymore. Every platform wants to know where you're going and get you there faster. Nobody's optimizing for the scenic route.
So consider this a small vote for the scenic route. Click around. Follow the boring link. See where it goes.
